309-13 a. Κίρκην ἑσπερίης: Apollonius followed those who place the wanderings of Odysseus in the Tyrrhenian sea, whose leader is Hesiod (Theog. 1015 sq.), saying that Circe dwelt in the aforementioned sea.
11 sch. IV 661 sch. κ 135 Strab. I 23. V 232
13 Hesiodi fg 66 Rz.²

b. ἑσπερίης εἴσω χθονός: Circe dwelt around Italy, whence the mountain Circeum, rich in drugs from her. Apollonius says, following Hesiod (see sch. a), that Circe came on the chariot of the Sun to the island lying off Tyrrhenia. He called it "western" because it lies towards the west.
17 cf. Hesiodi fg 67 Rz.²
319. 〈μειλιχίως:〉 gently, mildly. Lg

21 320. Et. Gen. (B) Αἰήτης: Αήτης, by addition of ι Αἰήτης. III 320.
321. 〈αὐτούς:〉 us. Sm

322. ποτὶ ξερόν: onto the dry land from the wet of the sea. The preposition ποτί is among the Dorians πρός, but among us and the Ionians it is used instead of παρά: Homer (Α 245) "and he cast the scepter to the ground."
and the Doric proverb "dragging the stone to the rope."
